title: 18 Days Without Leaving Home, Living Only on Internet Services | Day 4: What Do You Do When the Power Goes Out and You Fall Ill?
excerpt: This is not a contest to see who can stay home longest. QDaily Research Lab wants to find out whether the new wave of at-home services can actually give us a better life.
body:
This is not a contest to see who can stay home longest. QDaily Research Lab wants to find out whether the new wave of at-home services can actually give us a better life.

Today's theme: how to use internet services to handle "force majeure." What I didn't expect was to need the all-purpose Taobao so soon.

This is day four of the stay-at-home experiment ([details here](http://www.qdaily.com/articles/12983.html)). By spending 18 days without going out, we want to put today's popular at-home services through a hard test and see how much they can really improve our lives.

The trouble began last night.

Dinner started late. I was humming and washing the dishes when the lights went out and every appliance in the apartment stopped. Yes: living in an old residential compound, I hit the worst case. The prepaid electricity card had run out, and the power was cut in the middle of the night.

Luckily I wasn't alone. A few friends who had come over for dinner hadn't left yet. They offered to go down to the bank downstairs and see whether its self-service payment machine could top up the card; if it worked, I would "buy" their secondhand time on Xianyu, the secondhand marketplace. Meanwhile I opened Lakala Nearby Shop (Lakala Shenbian Xiaodian) to see whether a shop clerk could come to my door and collect the payment.

Neither worked. It was an old-style electricity card that Lakala couldn't read, and the bank's self-service machine sat in the lobby, which wouldn't open until the next morning.

![A darkened apartment during the power cut](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160801195221sIwzbteUyTEupA0h.jpg-w600)

Sitting on the balcony with a weak 4G signal and what little battery my phone had left, I posted on WeChat Moments asking friends to recommend a reliable errand-running service.

First I gave Youyou Little Secretary, the errand service that had let me down yesterday, another chance, asking whether this 24-hour online assistant could send someone to pay the electricity bill for me. Unfortunately the secretary replied: "I'm very sorry, that isn't possible. I can book a private car for you."

Fortunately, we still have the all-purpose Taobao. I typed in "Beijing errand running" and quickly found a seller who could help.

So I spent a night without power or internet. The new day arrived with a worsening case of acute pericoronitis around a wisdom tooth, and a headache that wouldn't go away.

### [Errand] Taobao | 14 minutes early

Ordered: 22:30; scheduled: 8:00; arrived: 07:46, 14 minutes early

Cost: service fee 50 yuan, electricity 95.6 yuan

![Chat with the Taobao seller](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160606004426cEXHwNTVfYSmPhsi.jpg-w600)*The Taobao seller replied very quickly*

Before 8 a.m., Mr. Sun was already knocking on my door. On his way over he had passed the bank and found it opened at 9, but he decided to get in line anyway. A little over an hour later, he had bought 200 kilowatt-hours of electricity for me.

Yet after the card went in, the apartment still had no power or internet. A neighbor passing by pointed out the problem: Mr. Sun found the circuit breaker beneath the meter box, and only then did my home come back to life.

This Taobao seller has run errands full time for several years. He has no team, but he drives his own car, so he can manage his own travel fairly well. Still, I hope that over the coming days there will be no more emergencies that only Mr. Sun can solve.

### [Medical] | Chunyu Doctor, online consultation

Lately it has poured in Beijing every night, and the weather has been fairly cool. Apart from not being able to work without internet, a night without power wasn't much of a hardship. What really caused trouble was my body acting up without warning.

I could have consulted my father, who is a doctor, over WeChat, but I wanted to see whether an app could solve it. The home medical service Diandianyi only sends people to give injections, nursing care or massage; it can't send a doctor to see you at home.

In fact, because of regulatory and policy limits, remote medicine is not a field entrepreneurs enter lightly. Dr. Zhang Qiang, who went from freelance practicing physician to founder, says his team's "Neighborhood Doctor" (Linjia Yisheng) official account only offers consultations; it cannot make diagnoses online.

Dingxiang Doctor's online medication consultation likewise only answers questions about how to use medicines, and does not diagnose online. In other words, if patients have been examined at a hospital and still have questions about their medication, they can get answers, but the online pharmacists won't tell you "what to do" about specific symptoms.

Next I tried Chunyu Doctor. Dr. Peng, from the oral and maxillofacial department of Suzhou Municipal Hospital in Anhui, answered my questions and recommended medication for the toothache, but said the headache wasn't necessarily caused by the wisdom tooth. I looked up the medicines he mentioned on Yaogeili, a medicine-delivery service, and got ready to order.

Before ordering, though, I posted the list in my family WeChat group. Once my parents, who both work in healthcare, approved it, I ordered painkillers, metronidazole and mouthwash on Yaogeili.

### [E-commerce] Benlai Life, fresh groceries | 2-day wait

Ordered: August 5, 01:40; delivered: August 6, 11:45

Cost: 116.9 yuan

![Groceries in three kinds of packaging](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160606004426YbIx2sMgTVcRFXpP.jpg-w600)*The groceries came in three kinds of packaging, depending on how they needed to be stored*

![Fresh groceries from Benlai Life](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160606004427ySKNn5OEM2viLxTR.jpg-w600)*Fresh groceries ordered from Benlai Life*

On the night of my second day indoors, a colleague talked me into trying a new dish, so I picked a fresh-food e-commerce site on a whim and ordered some ingredients. As it happens, that colleague and her mother are coming to visit this evening, so we can eat dinner together.

When the Weitepai courier knocked at noon, it took me a moment to work out what was going on. As far as I remembered, I had picked only a few items, yet the courier brought two fairly large boxes and two cartons of milk wrapped in plastic film.

The frozen items came in an insulated box with four ice packs. Inside the carton of chilled goods was a foam box and another four ice packs.

In short: what needed to stay cold stayed cold, and what needed to stay frozen stayed frozen.

### [Lunch] WeChat - Woody | 47-minute wait

Ordered: 10:57; delivered: 11:40; wait: 47 minutes

Cost: 77 yuan

![Ordering a Woody salad through WeChat](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160606004427hFTplbEysJDW4BHX.jpg-w600)*Ordering a Woody salad for delivery through WeChat*

Because of the power cut, the food I had kept in the fridge over the past few days had gone bad, and with all the fuss over the outage I had missed breakfast. Woody is a startup near the office that delivers salads, sandwiches and juices. After I ordered through its WeChat ordering system, the page promised delivery "as soon as possible."

The shop's own courier brought the order. Because it was cold food, it came in a kraft paper bag printed with the shop's logo, no different from picking up takeout myself.

Maybe it was the extra vitamin C, or maybe the anti-inflammatory pills I took after the meal, but by noon the day was starting to look less bad.

### [Medical] Yaogeili | 163-minute wait

Ordered: 11:42; delivered: 14:25, 103 minutes later than the promised one-hour delivery

Cost: 49 yuan, delivery fee waived

![Yaogeili medicine delivery](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160606004428fLuQkhHa2zygqjIm.jpg-w600)*Yaogeili buys medicine from a nearby pharmacy and brings it to your door*

Soon after I ordered, Yaogeili texted me that its "medicine delivery hero" was on the way. A little after 12, I checked the order status again: it said "completed," while I still had a headache, a toothache and no medicine.

I called the courier's number from the text. He apologized and said the system had assigned the order to him by mistake; he no longer delivered in my area, and after passing the order on to other couriers over WeChat, he had accidentally tapped "complete order." A while later I called Yaogeili's customer service line, and the agent said they would look into it.

In the end, my headache never got its painkillers. After resting all morning and taking the anti-inflammatory pills at noon, my symptoms had eased to a bearable level. By the time the medicine arrived, in a purpose-made black plastic bag that blocks light, I only needed some of it.

The courier who brought it told me they have three couriers covering a radius of 3-5 kilometers. He was new, so he couldn't tell me much more.

As it happened, a colleague of mine was at an event that afternoon where Yaogeili was also present. Yaogeili CEO Ren Bin told QDaily that the couriers are actually pharmacy staff, and that when a complaint like this comes in, the rules say the courier is fired on the spot, but the user receives no compensation.

I don't think firing a courier solves the problem. People in pain have especially little patience. Yaogeili has clearly made some efforts, such as standard packaging and a link to online medication consultations, but the next time I urgently need medicine, I may use another service.

### [Courier] SF Express | 126-minute wait

Ordered: 11:22; picked up: 13:28

Cost: 23 yuan

SF Express came to my home twice today. The first visit was a little after 9 a.m., bringing care packages from friends feeding me remotely: books, a Rubik's cube, a notebook and a handwritten card, reportedly picked out with his own paws by our Chief Cuteness Officer, Huahua (the handsome tomcat owned by the head of QDaily Research Lab).

Arriving right behind SF Express was a box of chocolates my colleagues had ordered on JD.com. All this kindness made me feel deeply loved. But the rules are the rules: the chocolates have to sit in the fridge for a dozen or so days, until the experiment is over.

![Gifts from the Shanghai office](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160606004428BJyGozcKusYW6vEl.jpg-w600)*Entertainment sent by colleagues at QDaily's Shanghai office*

![An SF Express waybill](http://img.qdaily.com/uploads/20160606004429pRM2T4Lt0C3yiJnc.jpg-w600)*The SF Express waybill*

Then I was told some documents needed to go to the Shanghai office, so I called a courier a second time. As usual, I ordered through the WeChat official account, and SF Express messaged me that the pickup had been accepted. This time, though, the courier was slower than usual.

The afternoon courier was not the one who had come in the morning. When I ship from the office, the waybill can be printed straight after ordering on WeChat. This time the courier said he could only fill in the waybill by hand, and when I asked whether I could pay with WeChat Pay, he said that would be difficult too.

In the end, I paid the shipping fee in cash.

### [Fitness] Keep

For the past few days colleagues have kept warning me: "When we finally see you again, don't be too weak to walk."

No need to worry. For two days in a row I've followed workouts on Keep, using the space I have at home. I chose two routines I can do in my hallway and on a yoga mat, and I exercise for at least half an hour a day. Tonight, before bed, I may still have time to jump along to one of Zheng Duoyan's workout videos.

In fact, having no time for the gym, or Beijing's air being too dirty to run in, is no excuse for sitting motionless in front of a computer. Last month I bought a membership card at the gym chain Quancheng Relian and ended up going three times. By that measure, judging only by how often I exercise, these days at home are healthier than the days I go out to work.

### Today's At-Home Tips

- Remote diagnosis still has many unsolved problems; if you feel unwell, see a doctor promptly.
- When working out at home, choose exercises that don't need much space. And if elderly people or small children who are easily disturbed by noise live below you, judge how hard to exercise by how well your building blocks sound.
- Day 4 total cost: 315.9 yuan
